answer: The smith forges each anchor at his anvil and stamps it with the yard's mark, and the stamp register holds the weight of every anchor. A hollow anchor claimed as forged fails the stamp: the iron must carry the smith's own mark at the echo of the shank, and an anchor never forged holds no ship at anchor. Faking an anchor means bribing the smith, forging twenty stamps and paying 17,800, while the oasis register is checked at every survey, so an anchor whose stamp was never entered is cut loose and lost.
